notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, site and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 6 simply supported 15-ft bays, W12X53 girders, one 3-ton pendant crane, on new freestanding W14X120 columns with welded twin-rib bracket seats, base plates, anchor rods and spread footings, and crane-level rod X-bracing; the existing building carries no crane load. Seismic: ordinary steel cantilever column system across the runway and rod bracing not specifically detailed for seismic resistance along it, Seismic Design Category B. The flexible plate cannot pass as sized (tie sizing ratio flange-tie-flange 1.23 > 1.00 for the estimated tie demands): the tie is paired flat bars on the same saddle, each bar taking half the force. A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves flange-tie-flange 1.03 for the estimated tie demands; a welded saddle is a Category D/E attachment on the top flange of this high-cycle runway (CMAA Class D, AIST Class C)): the tie is paired flat bars, which bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier.

aist.cycleSource: Fictitious example duty: 100,000 wheel-induced stress fluctuations in three duty bins (rated, half and light lifts), loaded and empty passes included. The bins are an assumed general-service proportion, not crane or owner data, so the fatigue checks govern by the all-cycle bound (the full fatigue load at every one of the 100,000 cycles); Miner's sum over the bins is listed for comparison until a sourced duty spectrum is entered.

Lightest compact W within the sizing targets (ratio ≤ 0.85, deflections ≤ 0.9 of the limits): top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 0.45, vertical deflection 0.38 and lateral 0.06 of their limits; flanges at least 8.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 27 by flange width; the next lighter, W21X50: flange 6.53 in narrower than the 8.50 in the details need. Configurator sizing ratios; the full calculation checks the section.

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints thermite or flash-butt welded by the rail supplier's qualified procedure (preheat, grinding, inspection); no joint bars or bolts.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
